incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion that disrupted multiple North American factory networks; attackers claim 8TB of data exfiltrated including chip drawings for Apple, Google, and NVIDIA orders.
incidents.impact: Several Foxconn factories in Wisconsin, Ohio, Texas, Virginia, Indiana and Mexico were forced offline; workers were sent home as Wi-Fi and computers failed. Foxconn says affected plants are resuming production.

incidents.vector: Repeat intrusion exploiting a flaw in Instructure's Free-For-Teacher accounts; after an initial breach on May 1, attackers defaced Canvas login pages on May 7 to launch school-by-school extortion.
incidents.impact: Names, emails, student IDs and messages from up to 275 million students and faculty across ~9,000 institutions were stolen. Canvas was pulled offline during final exams; Instructure paid a ransom and Congress opened an investigation.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a third-party IT services provider managing the victim's HPE Operations Agent platform, then abused signed enterprise management tools to push VBScripts, a malicious network provider DLL, and an LSA password filter to harvest cleartext credentials.
incidents.impact: Long-running stealthy intrusion (123+ days before IR engagement) achieved persistent domain controller access, credential interception during sign-ins and password changes, and lateral movement to sensitive assets — without traditional malware.

incidents.vector: Hundreds of malicious Ruby packages published over two days targeting RubyGems engineers and staff with XSS-style payloads designed to steal data from their systems.
incidents.impact: RubyGems disabled new user sign-ups while investigating; full scope of what attackers attempted to steal from staff is still being assessed. Incident unrelated to the concurrent TanStack/npm worm campaign.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion on May 4 stole data and encrypted systems used to ship, receive and manufacture injectable drug delivery components; no ransomware gang has yet claimed credit.
incidents.impact: Global business operations were disrupted; West shut down and isolated on-premise infrastructure and restored core enterprise systems, with manufacturing restored at some of 50 sites. Unit 42 hired for IR; data exfiltration scope still under investigation.

incidents.victim: TanStack, UiPath, MistralAI npm packages (downstream enterprises)
incidents.vector: Self-propagating 'Mini Shai-Hulud' worm exploited overly broad permissions in GitHub Actions workflows via an 'orphaned commit' to hijack CI/CD pipelines; cryptographically valid provenance signatures hid malicious payloads delivered through a concealed dependency.
incidents.impact: Roughly 400 npm packages including TanStack React Router (12M+ weekly downloads) were trojanized to steal AWS, GCP, GitHub, Kubernetes and HashiCorp Vault credentials, embed persistence in .vscode/ and .claude/ directories, and exfiltrate data via the Session anonymous messaging network.

incidents.vector: Phishing and malvertising campaigns delivered fake aviation software installers (including a poisoned SourceForge project) running a JavaScript RAT, PowerShell scripts, and LNK files abusing a Windows shortcut exploit (ZDI-CAN-25373).
incidents.impact: Campaign (tracked as HeartlessSoul / Versatile Werewolf) since at least September 2025 has exfiltrated GPS data, GIS shape files, digital terrain models and proprietary mapping files from Russian government and enterprise GIS workstations — yielding operational ground truth on Russian infrastructure.

incidents.vector: Internet-exposed API on Schemata's AI virtual training platform left publicly accessible without authentication, allowing unauthenticated retrieval of military records.
incidents.impact: US service member records and sensitive military training documents were exposed; Schemata took roughly 150 days to secure the leaky API after disclosure by Strix researchers.

incidents.vector: Intrusions into operational technology environments at multiple Polish water treatment plants; attackers reached industrial control systems at some facilities. Initial access vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Polish intelligence service ABW confirmed five water utilities were hacked over the past year, with ICS access in some cases. No public attribution to a specific group or foreign state, though the targeting profile suggests state-aligned activity.

incidents.vector: An attacker obtained root access to Huge Networks (a Brazilian DDoS-protection ISP) and the CEO's SSH keys, then weaponized the company's own infrastructure for DNS-reflection and amplification attacks against other Brazilian ISPs.
incidents.impact: Huge Networks unknowingly relayed massive sustained DDoS campaigns against the very Brazilian ISP customers it was contracted to protect; CEO blames competitor sabotage. Botnet built by mass-scanning insecure routers and open DNS resolvers.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained unauthorized access to Braintrust's AWS infrastructure and potentially the company's API key database.
incidents.impact: Braintrust — which provides AI observability tools to customers including Cloudflare, Vercel and Stripe — told customers to rotate API keys; downstream blast radius depends on customer key reuse and exposure.

incidents.vector: Distributed denial-of-service attack by hacktivist group The 313 Team — the same pro-Palestinian crew that recently took down Ubuntu/Canonical, BlueSky and Mastodon.
incidents.impact: Chime fended off the DDoS but customers filed a class-action lawsuit alleging service disruption. Demonstrates ongoing hacktivist DDoS-for-hire campaign against major consumer platforms.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised AVB Disc Soft's internal network and trojanized DAEMON Tools installers (signed with the vendor's legitimate certificate) starting April 8; first-stage backdoor profiled victims and selectively delivered the QUIC RAT to high-value targets.
incidents.impact: Thousands of users infected with first-stage beacon, but Kaspersky observed second-stage QUIC RAT deployed only to roughly a dozen government, scientific, manufacturing and retail organizations in Russia, Belarus and Thailand — consistent with prior Chinese supply-chain espionage TTPs (Notepad++, CCleaner).

incidents.vector: Social engineering attack tricked two DigiCert tech support employees into running a malicious .SCR (screensaver) file; CrowdStrike EDR on one host was misconfigured and offline from central management, letting the attacker dwell nearly two weeks.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole initialization codes for 60 in-flight Extended Validation code-signing certificate orders and weaponized 27 of them to sign Zhong Stealer malware (linked to Chinese e-crime group GoldenEyeDog / APT-Q-27). All implicated certificates revoked.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to Trellix's source code repositories; initial vector not disclosed publicly.
incidents.impact: Trellix says no changes were made to its products. The company — one of Europol's closest cybersecurity partners — notified law enforcement. Source code theft raises medium-term risk of bespoke evasion tooling against Trellix customers.

incidents.victim: CNAM — Moldova national health insurance agency
incidents.vector: Intrusion into Moldova's national healthcare database; no ransom demand, suggesting an intelligence-driven theft rather than financially motivated extortion. Moldovan cyber agency officials said Russian involvement cannot be excluded.
incidents.impact: Up to 30% of records affected by theft or restored-from-backup recovery. Database stores personal and financial information on every Moldovan adult or foreigner paying into the national insurance scheme, plus details of private medical providers — extremely sensitive amid Russian military threats against Moldova.

incidents.vector: Chinese actors compromised a Microsoft Exchange email server at the Cuban embassy and exfiltrated diplomatic email inboxes; same campaign reportedly hit more than 5,000 Exchange servers globally this year.
incidents.impact: Hackers gained visibility into Cuban diplomats' communications about the US naval blockade — actionable intelligence for Beijing given the Iran/Hormuz crisis and US military posture in the region.

incidents.vector: Lapsus$ leaked stolen Vodafone source code on its leak site after the company refused to pay an extortion demand. Initial access vector not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Source code for portions of Vodafone's EU operations was published, raising downstream risk of bespoke exploit development against Vodafone systems and customers.
